title: This Chinese Tea Costs $1.2 Million a Kilo — From 6 Bushes | China Travel Expert
description:
This Chinese tea is valued at around $1.2 million a kilogram. Here's why.

It's Da Hong Pao — "Big Red Robe" — a Wuyi rock oolong from Fujian. The rarest, priciest leaves come from just six "mother trees" that cling to a cliff hundreds of years old; together they yield under a kilo a year. In 1998, 20 grams sold at auction for 156,800 yuan. To protect them, picking the mother trees has been banned since 2006 — so the eye-watering price is really about six old bushes, not your cup.

🧭 Expert Tip: Skip the myth — any Wuyi tea shop sells excellent commercial Da Hong Pao oolong for a few dollars; it's the same style, just not mother-tree leaves.

全世界最贵的茶，只长在六棵树上——武夷山大红袍。
